<thought>We have the molecular ion at m/z 183.045 (likely [M+H]⁺), a ¹³C NMR showing nine distinct carbons: a carbonyl at 169.5 ppm, six aromatic carbons between 123–133 ppm, and two aliphatic carbons at 43.3 ppm (CH₂ attached to heteroatom) and 26.3 ppm (CH₃). This pattern suggests a phenyl ring bearing a single carbonyl group (carboxylic acid or ester) and an O‑CH₂‑CH₃ fragment. The formula that fits the mass and the carbon count is C₉H₁₀O₄ (neutral mass 182.038 Da, giving [M+H]⁺ 183.045). A structure consistent with this is **ethyl 4‑hydroxybenzoate** (para‑hydroxy‑ethyl benzoate). It contains a benzoate carbonyl (≈169 ppm), an aromatic ring (six signals), an O‑CH₂ (≈43 ppm) and a CH₃ (≈26 ppm), and matches the formula C₉H₁₀O₄.** 

Thus the SMILES string for ethyl 4‑hydroxybenzoate is: `CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(O)C=C1`.
